---

Three kinds of failure, split by **when** they bite:

| Kind | When | Who tells you | Cost to find |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[Compile Errors]] | before the program exists | `g++`, with a line number | cheap |
| [[Runtime Errors]] | while it is running | the program crashes | medium |
| [[Logic Errors]] | never | nobody | expensive |

The list runs in order of increasing pain, and that ordering is the point: the further
right a bug gets before you notice, the more it costs. Link errors sit between the first
two (the code compiled, the linker cannot find the definition); see [[Compile Errors]].

Finding them is [[debugging]], and the tool is a [[Driver]]. Not making them is
[[Program design]], [[Function design]], and writing the [[Algorithm]] down first.

The same three come back in [[Assembly Errors]] in [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]] and again as the
thing [[Unit testing]] exists to catch in [[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]]. It is
one taxonomy, used at every level of the degree.

It also came *before*, in [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE]], with one row changed:
**[[Python]] has no compile step**, so a syntax error is raised by the parser and the type
mismatches this table's first row catches at compile time become [[Runtime Errors]] instead. A
branch that never executes never reports its type error at all, which is the argument for
[[Test Coverage]].
